One declaration for both routes: a candidate DEPLOYMENT runs test-shard-<i> and doc-gate as pinned runs from the set's mw-core-tests image (/core-tests); a host PR/trunk run builds first and packs its own tree. Every shard reads the pack built from the run's own commit (--require-sha), never another set's. `restore` is what the host runs once per restore key, from the default branch's tip, to warm its shared NuGet cache with the build's closure. `parallel` lets a host run the stages after the build concurrently (fan-out: the 8 shards and doc-gate at once, as Actions' `test` matrix; the build runs alone). `owes` is what the stages still check less than dotnet-test.yml; ciEquivalent is refused while it is non-empty (check-build-stages.py, profile core).
owes: Consolidate test results: host-results (GitHub-hosted — core runs nothing on the self-hosted pool and reads no shared store) fetches each host shard's results tree over HTTPS by receipt (host-shard-results.py: the run's OIDC token, every file verified against its receipt) and uploads it as the `test` matrix's own artifact, but the build API serves receipts only, not their bytes — GET {api}/{repo}/{sha}/artifacts/{sha256} is owed by MeshWeaver.Plugins' BuildHostEndpoints, and until it answers that job is RED naming it. Paid only when collect-results consolidates results fetched that way (Actions: collect-results over the testResults-shard<i>-attempt<a> artifacts)

prepared packages: the build restores through the repository's nuget.config with the host's cache as the fallback folder, and a package the cache lacks is restored for the run and named; the host WARMS the cache from the default branch's tip by running the declared `restore` once per restore key (MeshWeaver.Deploy#68) - until that is on build-latest and has warmed core's key there, core's restore closure is not in the cache (Actions: the `build` job's NuGet-shelf hydration and restore)

browser: the shards that run browser tests need the headless browser and the font set the `browser-fonts` job stages and each `test` shard provisions; the build-host image (MeshWeaver.Deploy deploy/build-host/Dockerfile) carries neither

prepared mesh: on a host no test may install a mesh from scratch — a prepared mesh snapshot is cloned per run; which of core's fixtures that replaces is not established (owned by the prepared-server work)
evidence: no stage has run on a host — a probe of every stage on build-latest must be green and agree with the Actions legs of the same commit
